criteria.requirement: Models are represented as replaceable capabilities behind provider-independent ports.
No provider SDK type leaks into canonical domain/context/process contracts.
The same typed inputs and renderer version produce equivalent provider-facing prompt structure.
Conversation history is not implicitly injected.
Authority, user input, evidence, knowledge, memory and constraints remain distinguishable through rendering.
Serialization cannot promote untrusted content into Gateway authority.
Model routing is explicit, inspectable and bounded by capability and policy constraints.
No model is called when deterministic execution is sufficient.
Every model invocation carries an explicit output contract.
Model output is parsed and validated before becoming a Gateway result.
Schema, references, evidence and constraints can be verified independently of model confidence.
Optional model critics cannot be the sole acceptance authority.
Retry/fallback behavior is bounded and cannot expand scope or permissions.
Local SLM and remote/provider adapters can satisfy the same abstract capability where compatible.
Invocation provenance supports audit and replay without requiring chain-of-thought persistence.
Architecture, security and adversarial tests include prompt injection, malformed output, unsupported references, stale context and provider failure.
At least **95% coverage** for introduced/materially changed production code.
Stream fragments, malformed output and schema repair never trigger tool execution.
Tool proposals bind authorized inventory, arguments, scope, task and revision before host dispatch.
Invocation, repair and fallback consume the aggregate session budget; they cannot reset it.
Replay revalidates recorded outputs without redispatching external actions.
Deterministic rendering/validation claims are kept separate from probabilistic model generation.
Each EPIC-06 criterion maps to tests
two adapter paths pass conformance
fixture and live evidence are clearly labelled
deterministic replay cannot redispatch actions
failed gates block qualification.
Promotion gates use role-specific metric thresholds, not a single aggregate score.
Schema-valid but semantically wrong output can fail qualification.
Hallucination/unsupported-claim evidence is independently measured.
Confidence-bearing models have calibration evidence or confidence is treated as an uncalibrated signal.
Perplexity, when present, is labelled diagnostic and cannot independently pass a model.
Qualification evidence is revision-bound to model, tokenizer, runtime, profile and dataset.
Tokenizer identity and exact/estimated counting, complete payload/output reserve and typed context overflow
Generation controls are explicit and unsupported controls are denied
Cold/warm latency, throughput, CPU/RAM and applicable GPU/VRAM, token usage and failure/context behavior have independent gates
Sensitive data isolation and cancellation are adversarially tested
